subtopic: Language identity, Hinglish, regional pride and code-switching
passage: Note to parents, Nursery B. Chinmay, five, changes language without being asked. At pick-up he told Ajji in Marathi, "Mala bhook lagli." Two minutes later he asked his friend Sameer in Hindi, "Kal khelenge?" When I said, "Good afternoon, Chinmay," he answered, "Good afternoon, Sir," and showed me his drawing. He seems to sense what each person expects. I have not corrected him or asked him to choose one language. I told his Ajji that his switching is normal and healthy. Manoj, class teacher

qa.q: What did Chinmay say to Ajji at pick-up?
qa.a: Chinmay told Ajji in Marathi, "Mala bhook lagli."

qa.q: How does Chinmay seem to feel switching languages for each listener?
qa.a: Chinmay seems comfortable and at ease, switching language without being asked and even showing the teacher his drawing.

qa.q: What choice did the teacher make about Chinmay's switching, and why?
qa.a: The teacher did not correct him or ask him to pick one language, and told Ajji it is normal and healthy, so Chinmay can keep using all three.

qa.q: How might Ajji have felt when she heard the teacher's words?
qa.a: Probably reassured and proud, since the teacher said the switching is normal and healthy.

grounding: A child speaks one language to a grandparent, another to a friend and English at school without being told, sensing which language each person expects.

subtopic: Language identity, Hinglish, regional pride and code-switching
passage: In a village near Warangal, Hafsa, five, ran from her Nani's veranda to the lane. To Nani she said in Urdu, "Nani, paani do." To her friend Mahima at the well she called in Telugu, "Raa, aadukundam!" When the school van came, the teacher said, "Good morning, Hafsa," and Hafsa answered, "Good morning, Miss," and climbed in. Mahima giggled and shouted "Bye bye!" in English, and Hafsa waved from the window, already humming a Telugu song.

qa.q: Which language did Hafsa speak to Nani?
qa.a: Hafsa spoke Urdu to Nani, saying, "Nani, paani do."

qa.q: What might Hafsa be feeling as she hums a Telugu song in the van?
qa.a: Hafsa is probably happy and at ease, moving comfortably between the languages of her day.

qa.q: What choice does Hafsa make when the teacher greets her, and what does it show?
qa.a: Hafsa answers in English, "Good morning, Miss," showing that she senses which language the teacher expects without being told.

qa.q: How might Mahima feel about the languages she shares with Hafsa?
qa.a: Probably playful and at ease, since she giggles and shouts "Bye bye!" in English to her friend.

grounding: A child speaks one language to a grandparent, another to a friend and English at school without being told, sensing which language each person expects.
